attempts.prompt:
Create ONE character-only oil-painted reference folio, 1536 × 1024, landscape 3:2, on quiet warm ivory. Exact heading at UPPER LEFT: “PRINCESS DAZIEL”. Exact subtitle: “One Night's Mercy”.

The two supplied paintings establish PAINT HANDLING and restrained colour/value relationships ONLY. Do not depict their geography. Work in the Canadian Group of Seven / A. Y. Jackson observational oil tradition: large connected colour/value masses before texture, broad directional bristle strokes that describe form, selective substantial impasto, quieter connecting passages. The face must be as simply and materially painted as the coat. No smooth photorealistic face, glossy eyes, CGI modelling, uniform bevel-lit chips, golden flakes or cinematic rim lights.

Princess Daziel is an adult human woman, a grieving widow whose controlled fury turns into a difficult choice to save lives. She is physically capable, exhausted from six hours holding a lever in rain. Her explicit clothes are a quarry coat over hunting leathers and practical boots. She wears NO CROWN. For unspecified identity details, use a restrained consistent interpretation: early-thirties adult appearance, spare athletic build, warm light-medium olive skin, dark eyes and strong eyebrows, dark brown hair pulled into a practical short low braid, a firm unembellished face. No scars or magic marks invented. Heavy slate-grey thigh-length quarry coat with plain collar, muted brown hunting leathers beneath, dark work-worn boots, bare hands. Damp darkened cloth at shoulders/cuffs and a few loose wet hair strands convey story state without depicting rain or place. No royal jewellery, red cloak, sword, bow, quiver or plate armour.

Show THREE useful unclipped isolated full-body views: front three-quarter with coat partly open enough to show hunting leathers; side view with the same coat and proportions; rear three-quarter showing the practical braid and coat cut. Natural firm stance, no fashion posing. Arrange two compact head studies showing “Resolve” and “After the choice”: same woman, first controlled anger, second weary and grave, without a smile. Include selected isolated personal-tool details below: a small coil of hemp stay rope, one hand/forearm with rope loosely wrapped as in the source, a plain blunt iron release maul with wooden handle, and a compact hooded metal lantern. A folded plain writ can be tucked partly inside her coat, not displayed with invented readable text. Equipment must remain modest relative to the body; no huge weapon-like hammer. No quarry machinery or dragon.

Use soft cool-grey dawn daylight, broad muted light planes and connected charcoal/umber shadows. Light reveals wool, leather, skin, iron and rope without flooding or outlining every plane. Skin uses subdued earth/rose planes, coat blue-grey/charcoal, leather umber. No lantern glow or theatrical contrast.

Concise labels only: “Front”, “Side”, “Rear”, “Resolve”, “After the choice”, “Stay rope”, “Release maul”, “Hooded lantern”. No decorative prose. Absolutely NO locations, vignettes, landscape, background scene, floor/terrain patches, rocks, grass, trees, cast-shadow ground, other people, dragons, PAINT SWATCHES, colour chips or palette strips. All studies are cleanly isolated on ivory.
